chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shazaan, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the Qunut, so he said: (It is recited) in every obligatory and optional prayer.
ai.seo_question: When should Qunut be recited in Islamic prayers?
ai.summary: In this concise narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the permissibility and recommendation of Qunut in all prayers, reflecting the Shia view that it is a confirmed Sunnah rather than a strict obligation. This ruling underscores the spiritual significance of supplication as an integral component of both daily obligatory acts and voluntary devotions, highlighting the continuity between ritual action and divine communion.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abdul Rahman Bin Al Hajjaj, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘
I asked himasws about the Qunut, so heasws said: ‘(recite) in every Salāt, Obligatory as well in the optional’.
en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from ibn abu ‘Umayr, from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Hajjaj who has said the following:
“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about Qunut (supplication after recitation in second Rak‘at). He (the Imam) said, ‘It is in every Salah (prayer); obligatory or optional.’”
